transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-10-08
- Start: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 57 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Head of ML, Copperway), Olivia Park (CTO, Copperway), Jordan Mills (Platform Eng, Copperway)

Auto-generated summary (brief): We talked through Copperway's inference needs for a logistics assistant that generates route summaries, answers SLA questions, and interfaces with their internal toolchain. Main questions: context window size (session/history), multilingual throughput (English, Spanish, Portuguese), and whether to start on Hosted or jump to Dedicated/Private because of PII concerns.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick introductions — I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood team, and Diego our SE is here to run through performance and deployment options.
00:18 - Samir Patel: Yeah hi, thanks. I'm Samir, I lead ML at Copperway. We scrapped together the folks who actually run the infra — Olivia and Jordan.
00:28 - Olivia Park: hi all. quick agenda from our side: we want to understand model choices, and what it takes to go from POC to production. we have a few red lines around data residency and kms.
00:42 - Diego Alvarez: Great. we'll cover open models (we typically benchmark Llama-family, Mistral, and some 8k/32k context variants), plus Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private notes. feel free to interrupt.
01:05 - Jordan Mills: Quick context on infra: we run on GCP with VPC peering and private buckets, most of our workloads are in us-central1. we also have requirements for SSO via SAML, audit logs, and key management with Cloud KMS.
01:28 - Maya Chen: Perfect. Samir, could you give us the user flow and latency expectations?
01:35 - Samir Patel: Sure. The assistant will be used by customer support and ops. Typical flows are: short Q&A (one to three turns) under 1 second latency 95th would be ideal, but we can tolerate up to 2.5s for complex reranking. Then we have longer summarization jobs that can be asynchronous — those are fine at 5-10s. Context size: we often want full session history ~10k tokens, sometimes larger when pulling past invoices or manifests up to 40k. multilingual: roughly 70% EN, 20% ES, 10% PT.
02:10 - Diego Alvarez: OK that distribution helps. two quick callouts: 1) not every open model supports 40k natively — there are sparse-context variants and some models with extended windows but they tend to trade off latency/cost; 2) caching and prefix KV cache can reduce cost a lot for repeated prompts.
02:36 - Olivia Park: can you say whether Redwood Hosted supports VPC-like network controls? we can't send PII off-prem without controls.
02:44 - Maya Chen: Hosted supports strong tenant isolation and at-rest encryption but if you need VPC peering or private egress we usually recommend Dedicated or Private. we have a Private footprint for enterprise customers where control plane is in the customer's VPC and data stays on private network.
03:05 - Jordan Mills: That sounds promising. what's the delta in cost and ops between Hosted and Dedicated?
03:12 - Diego Alvarez: Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity — so predictable throughput and lower per-token unit cost at scale, but you pay for reserved nodes. Hosted is pay-as-you-go and faster to start, but unit cost can be higher if you hit sustained throughput. there's also a hybrid where you start Hosted and move heavy tails to Dedicated.
03:39 - Samir Patel: On models — we care about hallucination on contracts and manifests. Which open models have better factuality for that? we've seen Mistral do well on code/structural tasks, and Llama-2 derivatives strong for few-shot but hallucinate on company-specific entities.
04:02 - Diego Alvarez: factuality varies with fine-tuning, context engineering, and retrieval/tooling. in our benchmarks, tuned open variants with retrieval + tool-calling reduced hallucination by 40-60% vs base. also temperature and system prompt engineering matter.
04:22 - Olivia Park: so we'd likely need a retrieval layer hitting our document store, and tool calling into internal APIs — any limits there?
04:31 - Maya Chen: Redwood supports tool-calling patterns and structured output. for Private deployments we can enable internal tool integrations behind your VPC; for Hosted we provide secure webhooks with mTLS and auditable traces.
04:50 - Jordan Mills: about the 40k context — what's realistic? we've got some cases where we want to feed multiple manifests and conversations into a single prompt. is streaming KV cache practical?
05:01 - Diego Alvarez: For 40k you have two options: models that natively support extended context (32k/64k windows) or chunking plus retrieval with a local KV cache. streaming KV cache is supported in our runtime — it keeps token-level keys in GPU memory to avoid re-encoding prefixes each request. it's a big win for repeated context.
05:29 - Samir Patel: any numbers around cost? like 8k vs 32k per token? just rough order of magnitude?
05:35 - Diego Alvarez: ballpark: larger context models increase compute per request roughly linearly with sequence length on the attention cost; so 32k could be ~3-4x cost of 8k for same model family. but caching and batching change the picture. we'll send a detailed cost/latency matrix.
05:56 - Olivia Park: Compliance — we need SOC2, ISO, and evidence of KMS integration. Redwood has SOC2, right?
06:05 - Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we also have ISO 27001 docs. we support KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys in Private. I'll attach the security pack after the call.
06:20 - Jordan Mills: What about SSO — SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
06:24 - Maya Chen: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning roles; RBAC can be integrated with your identity provider.
06:34 - Samir Patel: Let's get into the model comparison — can you run through example candidates and tradeoffs?
06:40 - Diego Alvarez: Sure. short list we propose for your workload: 1) Mistral-X (8k/32k variants) — good cost/accuracy balance, strong multilingual base; 2) Llama-deriv fine-tuned (various quantized sizes) — flexible and fast, but needs safety/factual fine-tuning; 3) OpenChain-extended (32k) — good for long context but higher cost. For hallucination-sensitive tasks we recommend pairing base models with retrieval and a reranker.
07:12 - Olivia Park: Do any of these have built-in tool-calling or do we need to implement wrappers?
07:17 - Diego Alvarez: Tool-calling is implemented at the Redwood runtime layer. models don't need to natively support it; we provide a structured tool-call API that your backend can implement. function hints and schema enforcement are supported.
07:33 - Samir Patel: What about quantization — we want to reduce cost without losing accuracy. how aggressive can we go?
07:38 - Diego Alvarez: Our Optimize tooling recommends quantization profiles — 4-bit/8-bit quant at inference has different regressions by model. for many classification and routing tasks 4-bit is fine; for abstractive summarization we often recommend 8-bit or mixed precision to preserve fluency. we can give model-specific guidance after running a small eval.
07:57 - Jordan Mills: latency SLOs — you mentioned batching helps throughput but hurts p99. can Redwood do dynamic batching policies per route?
08:06 - Maya Chen: Yes, per-route policies exist. you can set strict latency SLOs for interactive routes with small batch sizes and allow larger batching on async routes to save cost. autoscaler works with these policies.
08:22 - Olivia Park: For a pilot, we'd like to see: 1) a Hosted quickstart to validate accuracy and tail latency on our prompts; 2) a Dedicated benchmark if Hosted doesn't meet 95th latency under load. is that reasonable?
08:35 - Maya Chen: Totally. typical path is Hosted rapid POC (2-3 weeks) then Dedicated pilot for predictable load. if you're highly regulated we can run Private from day one but that adds procurement time.
08:49 - Samir Patel: Procurement time — how long to spin up Private? we don't want months of procurement before testing.
08:56 - Diego Alvarez: Private deployments often take 6-8 weeks due to network and security stamping; Dedicated can be as fast as 2-4 weeks depending on region and commit. Hosted is immediate.
09:12 - Samir Patel: On benchmarks, could you run a sample 50 concurrent users hitting Q&A and summarization flows? we want p95 numbers and cost per 1k tokens.
09:22 - Diego Alvarez: Yes we'll provision a small benchmark harness. we'll need your representative prompt set and expected concurrency distribution.
09:30 - Jordan Mills: We'll provide logs next week. what about data retention and audit logs for Hosted? we need to be able to purge and to show who called what.
09:39 - Maya Chen: Hosted stores logs per tenant; retention and purge policies can be configured. for audit-grade requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private where we can route logs to your SIEM.
10:01 - Olivia Park: Anything about offline encryption, HSM? we want customer-managed keys.
10:06 - Diego Alvarez: In Private we support HSM/KMS and can integrate with your cloud KMS; in Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys options too. Hosted supports server-side encryption with provider-managed keys by default, with customer-managed options on enterprise plans.
10:28 - Samir Patel: Let's talk multilingual performance — do you have per-language benchmarks?
10:34 - Diego Alvarez: Yes, we maintain per-model evals for EN/ES/PT. some models drop more in PT than EN; Mistral-X showed steady performance across ES/PT in our tests, but we'll share exact evals.
10:48 - Olivia Park: For integration, we need tool-calling to call internal APIs (shipment lookup, ETA). can we restrict scope of tools and audit calls?
10:56 - Maya Chen: You can scope tool access by role and by route. calls are logged; for Private deployments calls never traverse public internet.
11:12 - Samir Patel: Any patterns for reducing hallucination with tool-calls?
11:16 - Diego Alvarez: Yes — canonical approach: 1) retrieval to ground facts, 2) tool-calling for authoritative answers (e.g., shipment API), 3) a reranker or deterministic fallback to an exact-match response when confidence low.
11:36 - Jordan Mills: curious about cost modeling — how detailed is the pricing? do you break out per-token + per-request overhead + reserved node costs?
11:45 - Maya Chen: Pricing breaks out per-token generation and embedding units, per-request overheads, and Dedicated reservation pricing. we'll send a sample TCO spreadsheet against your expected monthly tokens.
12:01 - Olivia Park: Security checklist on our side: SOC2 docs, KMS integration guide, networking diagram for Private, SAML/SCIM details. can you provide those?
12:11 - Maya Chen: Yes, I'll attach the security pack and a VPC design doc.
12:18 - Samir Patel: What are typical success criteria for moving from pilot to production?
12:23 - Diego Alvarez: Typical criteria: stable 95th latency within SLO, hallucination reduction to acceptable rate on evaluation prompts, pass security checklist, and a cost per active user within targets.
12:37 - Jordan Mills: I'd like to book a technical deep dive with Diego to go through the benchmark harness and the KV cache mechanics.
12:43 - Diego Alvarez: Happy to — we can demo live KV cache behavior and run a canary against a small set of production-like data.
12:51 - Maya Chen: Recap and action items: we'll send model perf matrix, security docs, and pricing spreadsheet. Diego will create the benchmark repo and sample scripts. Copperway will send anonymized prompt logs and a prioritized list of routes to test. Pilot plan: 3 weeks Hosted POC, then evaluate Dedicated pilot if needed.
13:20 - Olivia Park: Sounds good. timeline-wise we'd like the Hosted POC to start by 2027-10-18.
13:28 - Maya Chen: We'll aim for that. I'll try to get the docs out by end of day tomorrow.
13:35 - Samir Patel: Great. thanks everyone.
13:38 - Meeting ends.

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcription occasionally merged technical acronyms (KMS -> K M S) and mis-typed model names (Mistral-X may appear as 'Misa rol x'). there are natural pauses and some crosstalk.

Attachments referenced: security_pack_v2.pdf (link sent after call), perf_matrix_template.xlsx, benchmark_repo (invitation to be sent).
